For *short-circuit* situation - [~accountid:6215e9f275803500683497d5] will send the behavior data/graph of “Charger FB”  for [~accountid:6125f202da0c1a0068892700], so that he can implement some logic to identify a short-circuit situation specifically, so that in that situation the charger output can be turned off for the remainder.

For *loose/intermittent charger output* situation - we brainstormed, that in this situation the RFID should not immediately switch off the charger output and consider it as faulty, but instead keep it on for a certain amount of time (1-2 minutes). If during this time:

* “Charger FB” is constantly off for 1-2 minutes, then the charger will be switched off.
* “Charger FB” is intermittently on-off throughout this 1-2 min cycle AND there is no distinctive short circuit behavior from the “Charger FB”, then the charger will not be switched off. 

This will combat the situation where there is no short-circuit, but there may be intermittent bad connection between the socket and scooter adapter. Note that the 1-2 minutes is an example, this must be agreed upon first with [~accountid:6113cc923900e600705bdd88] .

For *no load-no “Charger Enable”* situation - [~accountid:5e9a112618b8ed0c0f776390] must determine whether 1 second interval is enough delay for the RFID, or if some scooters need a longer delay (charger not getting load during the 1 minute).

For *RFID LED behavior* situation - [~accountid:5e9a112618b8ed0c0f776390] and [~accountid:6113cc923900e600705bdd88] must agree on what kind of LED behavior is expected in each of the situations above.
